title: From Fall to Festive: November Happenings Near Massanutten
seo_title: November Events Near Massanutten | The Valley Edit
subtitle: November Happenings & Local Favorites in the Shenandoah Valley

hero.alt: Autumn foliage on the ridge above the Shenandoah Valley under a blue sky

intro: There's something special about November in the Shenandoah Valley. The mountains are settling into their late-autumn colors, local markets are filling with handmade treasures, and the first holiday lights are beginning to appear.

From a morning spent discovering local artisans to Thanksgiving traditions and festive evenings at Massanutten, November offers plenty of reasons to make a little more time for the people and places you love.
Here's what we're looking forward to this month.

items.title: Festive Fall Open-Air Market
items.place: Green Valley Book Fair, Mount Crawford
items.desc: Shop more than 50 local vendors featuring handmade goods, art, books, and seasonal treats. A wonderful excuse to start holiday shopping early.

items.title: Burg Bash
items.desc: Celebrate the season of gratitude with an afternoon of family-friendly games, attractions, music, candy, and community fun.

items.title: Light Up the Park Begins
items.desc: Welcome the holiday season with sparkling lights, music, s'mores by the firepit, and festive fun. Santa appearances are scheduled for select nights.

items.title: Holiday Card-Making Workshop
items.place: Friendly City Clay & Art Center, Harrisonburg
items.desc: Create hand-printed holiday cards at a beginner-friendly linocut workshop. Open to ages 16 and older; advance registration and a workshop fee apply.

items.title: Rocktown Turkey Trot
items.desc: Start Thanksgiving with a little movement and a lot of community spirit. The annual event features a four-mile race and a special Gobble Gobble Kids Dash.

items.title: Deck the Halls Christmas Market
items.desc: Celebrate Small Business Saturday with holiday shopping, handmade gifts, fresh wreaths, baked goods, and family photo opportunities. Admission is listed at $5 per adult, with children admitted free.

in_season.title: A Slower Kind of Saturday
in_season.lead: Before the holiday rush begins, make time for a little local tradition.
body: The Harrisonburg Farmers Market is open Tuesdays and Saturdays throughout November, offering an easy way to explore the area's growers, makers, and small businesses.
Wander through Turner Pavilion, browse what's in season, and pick up something local to enjoy during your stay.
The market's November schedule includes Tuesday and Saturday markets from 8 AM–1 PM.
Whether you're planning breakfast, shopping for a holiday gathering, or simply enjoying a morning downtown, it's a lovely way to experience Harrisonburg beyond the usual attractions.

image.caption: Harrisonburg Farmers Market (file photo)

featured.title: Handmade for the Holidays
featured.event: Festive Fall Open-Air Market at Green Valley Book Fair
body: There's something about finding a gift at a local market that makes it feel a little more meaningful.
This November, Green Valley Book Fair brings together more than 50 local businesses, artists, crafters, and bakers for its Festive Fall Open-Air Market.
Expect everything from handmade jewelry and home décor to artwork, accessories, and sweet treats.
And because the market takes place outside Green Valley Book Fair, it's the perfect opportunity to browse the book fair's collection of discounted books, puzzles, and gifts while you're there.
featured.why: It combines holiday shopping, local creativity, and a little something for nearly everyone—without requiring a packed itinerary.
featured.close: Make a morning of it, enjoy lunch, and leave room for an afternoon of exploring the valley.

eat.title: A Little Taste of November
eat.lead: Good food deserves a place in the itinerary, especially when a local market makes it easy to sample something new.

body: That means you can work a savory bite, something to sip, and a sweet finish into your market visit without needing to make several separate stops.
For another low-key food outing, stop by the Harrisonburg Farmers Market and see what its seasonal vendors have available.
eat.tip: Come hungry, browse first, and make time for dessert. Vacation calories have a remarkable talent for finding their own itinerary.

detour.title: Get Creative at Friendly City Clay
detour.lead: Holiday shopping is fun. Making something yourself? That's a different kind of memory.
detour.chip: Nov 21 · 1–3 PM · Linocut Card Making: Holiday Greetings
body: At Friendly City Clay & Art Center in Harrisonburg, creative workshops offer visitors a chance to slow down, try something new, and leave with a piece of the experience.
On November 21 from 1–3 PM, the studio has scheduled Linocut Card Making: Holiday Greetings, a beginner-friendly workshop where participants ages 16 and older can create hand-printed holiday cards.
It's a particularly nice option for couples, friends, or anyone looking for an afternoon activity beyond the slopes.
Friendly City Clay is also one of Cedar Escape's local experience partners, with a guest benefit available on eligible scheduled workshops.
detour.note: Workshop availability and discount eligibility should be confirmed before booking.

ahead.title: A Little Holiday Magic Is Coming
ahead.lead: November is just the beginning. If you're already thinking about a December mountain getaway, here are a few experiences worth putting on your calendar.

items.title: Light Up the Park
items.desc: Massanutten's seasonal light experience returns on select nights, making it an easy addition to a winter stay.

items.title: Winter Wonderfest
items.desc: Downtown Harrisonburg celebrates with festive activities, holiday shopping, performances, and seasonal family fun. The city's Holiday Parade begins at 7 PM.

items.title: JMU HolidayFest
items.desc: Celebrate the sounds of the season with performances by JMU's Choral Area and Wind Symphony at the Forbes Center for the Performing Arts.

ahead.next: Our next edition of The Valley Edit will explore these celebrations and more in Holiday Magic in the Shenandoah Valley.

closing.title: Make Room for More Memories
body: A weekend in the Shenandoah Valley deserves more than a hurried day trip.
After exploring local markets, enjoying holiday traditions, and discovering the area's hidden gems, return to Cedar Escape—a spacious five-bedroom retreat inside Massanutten Resort.
Gather for a movie, enjoy the game room, soak in the hot tub, or simply make time to be together.
Because sometimes the best part of a getaway is having nowhere else you need to be.
